thread.title: Data center a first step in Goodyear's quest for tech companies

author: Patrick O'Grady
title: Data center a first step in Goodyear's quest for tech companies
text: – Managing Editor, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 9, 2019, 4:00am MST Vantage Data Centers is building a three-building facility in Goodyear in a move the southwest Valley city hopes will be a springboard to landing more technology companies. Santa Clara, California-based Vantage said Tuesday it was bringing a campus to a 49-acre parcel on the southeast corner of Van Buren Street and Bullard Avenue that it purchased for $12.76 million . For the city, which has sought to broaden its employment base for the past several years, the move is seen as a positive first step, said Goodyear Mayor Georgia Lord. "It behooves us to have them commit to coming to Goodyear," she said. Vantage officials said the plan is to build three buildings on the campus totaling 160 megawatts of data center operations. The first building will be 32 megawatts and is slated to open in 2020. “This newest development in the Southwest is an ideal location for our customers due to its tax incentives, low power costs and rich connectivity," said Sureel Choksi , president and CEO of Vantage Data Centers, in a statement. Arizona offers incentives to data center developers providing the project is more than $50 million of capital improvements. Vantage officials said it was too early in the process to comment on buildout costs for the campus. Vantage has other data center facilities in California, Virginia and Washington. Looking to attract developers For Goodyear, the move is the first in what it hopes will be more technology companies locating along Bullard Avenue, which the city is designating as a technology corridor in an effort to attract developers, said Lori Gary , the city's economic development director. Currently, significant vacant parcels along Bullard between Maricopa County 85 and Interstate 10 are available for development. The city has worked with Arizona Public Service Co. to beef up its electric infrastructure to handle data centers and other tech companies. It also has access to a fiber optic corridor along MC 85 that will bolster connections, Gary said. The city has talked with developers in terms of turning some of that vacant land into offices to lure in tech companies, Gary said. "There is certainly a shortage of high-tech, class A office space [in the West Valley], and we want to be at the forefront of developing that," she said. Goodyear has made inroads to some tech development in terms of online distribution centers, primarily centered on Loop 303 north of Indian School Road. Companies operating in the area include Dick's Sporting Goods, outfitter REI, pet goods supplier Chewy.com and others. While Vantage is the first confirmed data center, Microsoft Corp. was the first large tech company to enter Goodyear in September 2018 when it paid $48 million for 272 acres near MC 85 and Lower Buckeye Road. The city, which has not said what is planned for the site or that Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT) is even involved, approved a rezoning for the land that would allow uses consistent with a data center. The Valley is a hub for data centers in large part because the region is a nexus for fiber lines that cross the country and its lack of potential natural disasters that could cause power or network disruptions. Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) has a large data center in Mesa and several companies, such as Iron Mountain and CyrusOne Inc. (Nasdaq: CONE) have built massive data centers, but primarily in the East Valley. – Managing Editor, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 9, 2019, 4:00am MST Related Content
